rules.statement: When an authorization error cannot be safely redirected (invalid or unregistered redirect_uri, unresolvable client_id), never redirect to the untrusted URI; show the error to the resource owner directly instead.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §3.1.2.4 requires the OP not to redirect to an untrusted URI and says it SHOULD inform the resource owner.
rules.check: Look for authorize-endpoint error paths that redirect to a redirect_uri that was not validated, or that redirect when client_id could not be resolved.

rules.statement: Keep IResult types in abstractions packages thin: ExecuteAsync resolves an IResultExecutor<TResult> from DI and delegates to it, and serialization, Accept parsing and formatter lookup live in the core implementation.
rules.why: Putting the plumbing inside a public result type in a lean abstractions package couples it to specific response types and representations.
rules.check: Look for an IResult.ExecuteAsync in an Abstractions project that serializes JSON, parses Accept headers or picks formatters inline instead of delegating to an executor.

rules.statement: Support alternate response representations through an open collection of formatter strategies. Each formatter declares the media types it emits and a CanFormat predicate, and is registered with TryAddEnumerable. Do not add type checks or media-type checks inside the result type.
rules.why: An inline branch favors one response type and one media type. With the open collection, a new representation is an additive registration.
rules.check: Look for code like `if (response is SomeError && prefersHtml)` inside result or executor code, or a new single-purpose renderer seam for one response type.

rules.statement: Implement the default representation (for example JSON) as a formatter registered in the same pipeline as the alternates, and make it the final fallback candidate in negotiation.
rules.why: The default body then goes through the same pipeline rather than a special-cased branch, so a wildcard or non-matching Accept still resolves to it.
rules.check: Look for a default JSON body written in an inline fallback branch outside the formatter collection, or negotiation that has no final default candidate.

rules.statement: In server-driven content negotiation, choose a non-default formatter only when Accept lists an explicit type/subtype it supports. Wildcard-only Accept values such as */* must get the default representation.
rules.why: This keeps negotiation safe by default: JSON stays the OAuth/OIDC wire default for curl and other programmatic callers unless an interactive client asks for something else.
rules.check: Look for negotiation that lets */* or type/* match an HTML or other alternate formatter.

rules.statement: Write HTML response bodies with HttpResponse.WriteAsync(text, SecureEncoding.UTF8, cancellationToken) from NCode.Buffers, following the existing HTML executor idiom.
rules.why: This reuses the established NCode.Buffers writing stack.
rules.check: Look for HTML bodies written with Encoding.UTF8, by manually encoding into byte arrays, or through other ad-hoc writers.

rules.statement: Optional alternate representations registered by an optional package must degrade gracefully: when no formatter is registered, the response falls back to the default representation without error.
rules.why: Hosts without the interactive package must still get valid JSON error responses.
rules.check: Look for code that throws or fails when no alternate formatter is registered, or that makes core code depend on the optional package.
